Deadly bus crash shuts down the Thruway

New York State Police say there are multiple fatalities, entrapments, and injuries

PEMBROKE, N.Y. — A tour bus carrying more than 50 passengers from  Niagara Falls to New York City crashed and rolled over Friday afternoon  on the New York State Thruway near Pembroke, killing and injuring  multiple people, according to State Police.

The crash happened when the bus lost control just before the Pembroke  exit. Passengers were thrown from the vehicle as windows shattered.

"At this time we have multiple fatalities, multiple entrapments and  multiple injuries," Trooper James O’Callahan, a spokesperson for the New York State Police, said at the scene.

O’Callahan said the bus was traveling eastbound when "for unknown  reasons the vehicle lost control, went into the median, overcorrected  and ended up in the ditch, which would be on the right side of the  roadway." The driver survived the crash.

Police said many of the passengers were from India, China, and the Philippines. Translators were being brought in to assist.

Emergency crews responded with multiple ambulances and at least six  medical helicopters. Mercy Flight deployed all three of its helicopters.

Erie County Medical Center reported treating at least eight patients  by 2:10 p.m. Additional patients were transported to hospitals across  the region. ECMC officials said there were "several fatalities at the  scene."

Kaleida Health said Friday it received 20 patients across three of  its hospitals following the tragic bus accident on Interstate 90.

Buffalo General admitted four adults, all in good condition, with one person already discharged, according to the health system.

Millard Fillmore Suburban Hospital received 13 patients — 11 adults  and two children — with 10 reported in good condition and three listed  in fair condition.

Oishei Children’s Hospital treated three children — two in good condition and one in serious condition.

In a statement, Kaleida Health expressed appreciation for emergency personnel who responded to the crash.

"We are grateful to local law enforcement and first responders for  their quick action on the scene and a special thank you to our staff and  providers who are actively caring for these patients,” the statement  read.

Hospital officials emphasized that staff routinely prepare for emergencies of this scale.

Heavy Rainfall Warning No. 8 #NCR_PRSD
Weather System: Southwest Monsoon (Habagat)
Issued at: 8:00 AM, 23 August 2025(Saturday)

YELLOW WARNING LEVEL: Bataan and Zambales(Olongapo, Subic, San Marcelino, Castillejos, San Narciso, San Antonio, San Felipe, Cabangan, Botolan).
ASSOCIATED HAZARD: Possible FLOODING in flood-prone areas.
Meanwhile, expect light to moderate with occasional heavy rains over Pampanga, Tarlac and Zambales(Candelaria, Iba, Masinloc, Palauig, Santa Cruz) within the next 3 hours.
Light to moderate with occasional heavy rains affecting Rizal, Batangas(Laurel, Tanauan, Santo Tomas, Talisay, Malvar, Balete, Lipa, Mataasnakahoy, San Jose, Ibaan, Cuenca, Batangas City, San Pascual, Alitagtag, Bauan, Mabini, Taal, San Luis, Santa Teresita, San Nicolas, Agoncillo, Taysan, Lemery, Rosario, Padre Garcia, San Juan, Lobo), Bulacan(Norzagaray), Quezon(General Nakar), Metro Manila(Taguig, Paranaque, Muntinlupa, Las Pinas), Laguna(Calamba, Los Banos) and Cavite(General Trias, Imus, Bacoor, Kawit, Noveleta, Rosario, Cavite City, Dasmarinas) which may persist within 3 hours and may affect nearby areas.

The public and the Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Offices concerned are advised to MONITOR the weather condition and watch for the next warning to be issued at 11:00 AM today.
